title: Mod Content Override File
description: Shape of a mod's Content/buildings.json, Content/units.json and Content/resources.json, and of a scenario's buildingsOverrideFile / unitsOverrideFile / resourcesOverrideFile. Entries are matched to the base game by id (case-insensitive). Files apply in load order: every active mod alphabetically by mod id, then the active scenario's override file. Base entries are never removed from the game's data: an id that a replace-mode roster does not list, or that a "disabled" list names, is switched off instead (hidden from build and recruit menus, never seeded, never chosen by the AI, rejected by the build command), which keeps saves and multiplayer consistent.

oneOf.description: A bare array of entries: merge mode.

mode.description: "merge" (default): entries change or add to the base game. "replace": the entries ARE the roster — every base id they do not list is disabled. "replace" with no entries starts from scratch. A later replacing file discards what earlier files composed.

replace.description: Alias for "mode": "replace". Do not combine with a contradicting "mode".

overrides.description: The entries. The Mod Builder writes this key; "buildings", "units" and "resources" (the base config's own root keys) are accepted too.

disabled.description: Ids switched off in this game. Wins over being listed.

id.description: Base id to change, or a new id to add. Unit ids must fit 29 bytes, building ids 61.

inherit.description: For an id that exists in the base game: true overwrites only the fields this entry names; false makes this entry the whole definition (missing fields take engine defaults). Defaults to false in a replace-mode file and true otherwise. New ids are always whole definitions.
